question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom / Phrase.

To sit at someone's feet

options.text: To attend upon as someone's disciple

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. To attend upon as someone's disciple.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"To sit at someone's feet"** means to be a devoted follower or disciple of someone, often a mentor or a teacher. (किसी के शिष्य बनना)

 
 
• **Example: **Many young musicians wish to sit at the feet of a great master like Ravi Shankar to learn the intricacies of classical music.
 
 
 
• **To attend upon as someone's disciple** implies being a dedicated student or follower who learns and respects the teachings of a mentor. (किसी के शिष्य के रूप में उपस्थित होना)
 
 
• **Example: **He spent years attending upon the feet of his guru, absorbing every lesson and wisdom imparted.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. To attend upon as someone's disciple.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To wash someone's feet **(किसी के पैर धोना): Literally means to clean someone's feet, often as a sign of respect or servitude.

 
 
• **Example:** In many cultures, washing someone's feet is a sign of humility and respect.
 
 
 
• **To be someone's equal **(किसी के बराबर होना ): To be on the same level in terms of status, ability, or rank.
 
 
• **Example: **Despite his young age, he proved to be his mentor's equal in terms of skill and knowledge.
 
 
 
• **To be proud of someone** (किसी पर गर्व करना): To feel pride due to someone's achievements or qualities.
 
 
• **Example:** She is very proud of her son's accomplishments in the field of medicine.
